'''Tyler Quincy Dorsey''' (alternate [[Greek language|Greek]] spelling: Τάιλερ Κουίνσι Ντόρσεϊ, Tailer Kouinsy Ntorsey)<ref>[http://www.fibaamericas.com/en/box.asp?g=55&n=A&r=11715&t=KGZJCFHHHD TEAM LEADERS Greece Ntorsey, Tailer Kouinsy.]</ref><ref>[http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Tailer-Kouinsy-Ntorsey/Summary/108124 Tailer Kouinsy Ntorsey Nationality: Greece.]</ref><ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/compID_UIfgjyQcGqk-fPlnl66Tj0.season_2016.roundID_12474.teamID_291.html GREECE ROSTER Tailer Kouinsy Ntorsey.]</ref> (born February 14, 1996) is a Greek-American [[basketball]] player. After graduating from [[Maranatha High School]], in [[Pasadena, California]], he played college basketball for the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Ducks]]. He is also a member of the senior [[Greek national basketball team|Greek national team]].

== High school ==
Dorsey initially attended [[St. John Bosco High School]], in the city of [[Bellflower, California]]. In his [[sophomore]] season, he began to establish himself as a solid scorer, with a 17.0 [[Point (basketball)|points]] per game scoring average. He made a big impact afterwards, where, as a [[Eleventh grade|junior]], he managed to win the State Championship, and was the star of the team, averaging 21.4 [[Point (basketball)|points]] per game, 6.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 4.7 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] per game. 

In his senior year, he decided to transfer to [[Maranatha High School|Maranatha]], due to his desire to return to his hometown of [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]], for his final year. He was a standout player there, where he dazzled with his scoring and [[Athleticism|athletic abilities]]. He averaged 34.0 [[Point (basketball)|points]] per game, to go along with 10.4 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 3.7 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], and 1.9 [[Steal (basketball)|steals]] per game. 

Together with his second state championship win, he earned the 2015 Gatorade State Player of the Year for [[California]] award. He had many impressive games, like the one where he scored 52 points, in an 85-60 [[Win (baseball statistics)|win.]] He was able to be efficient in every game, shown by the fact that he finished in double figures in scoring all 30 of his games played. Despite being considered the 23rd best player of his age group, he was not selected to play in the [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald’s All-American Game]]. He initially committed to play [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Arizona]], but he changed his mind, and then committed to [[University of Oregon|Oregon]], instead, on 2 February, 2015.

== College career ==

=== Freshman Year ===
Dorsey played his first [[official game]] as an [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon Duck]], in the season opener against [[Jackson State Tigers basketball|Jackson State]], where [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] won; and he was declared the [[Most Valuable Player|MVP]] of the game, after scoring 20 [[Point (basketball)|points]] for his team, in an 80–52 win. Dorsey missed two games in the middle of the [[Season (sports)|season]], due to an [[injury]], but he soon came back into form. He scored a career-high 25 [[Point (basketball)|points]] against rivals [[Oregon State Beavers men's basketball|Oregon State]], in an 91–81 win. 

The [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Ducks]] won the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] [[Season (sports)|regular season]] and [[2016 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2016 Conference Tournament]]. In the [[2016 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament#Bracket|tournament final]] against the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|University Of Utah]], Dorsey's team, Oregon, dominated, and beat Utah by a score of 88–57. Oregon's 31-point margin of victory was the largest in the Pac-12 Championship game's history. Dorsey had a stellar performance, being the top scorer, with 23 points, and having also grabbed 9 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. He was picked for the [[2016 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament#All-tournament team|All-Tournament Team]], and was the tournament's top scorer. 

Oregon earned the top seed in the West region, and went as the number one team of their conference into [[March Madness 2016|March Madness]]. After the season, Dorsey was one out of 162 early-entry candidates that initially declared for the [[2016 NBA draft]].<ref>[http://registerguard.com/rg/sports/34310794-81/tyler-dorsey-dillon-brooks-officially-declare-for-nba-draft.html.csp Tyler Dorsey, Dillon Brooks officially declare for NBA Draft.]</ref> However, he ultimately withdrew before the draft withdrawal deadline.<ref>[http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2016/05/dillon_brooks_and_tyler_dorsey.html Dillon Brooks and Tyler Dorsey withdraw from NBA Draft, return to Oregon Ducks.]</ref>

=== Sophomore Year ===
Dorsey helped the [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Ducks]] to the finals of the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|Pac-12 conference tournament]], and he was named to the [[2017 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Tournament#All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]]. Later, in the [[2017 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA tournament]], Dorsey hit numerous shots down the stretch against the [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|University of Rhode Island]] and the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]], to lead his team to the [[2017 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament#Final Four|Final Four]]. Oregon was finally defeated by the eventual champions, the [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina Tar Heels]].

== National team career ==
Dorsey was originally cut from a [[USA Basketball]] tryout camp for its [[USA national under-19 basketball team|Under-18 national team]] in 2014. The next year, before the [[2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]] began, he was invited to [[Greece men's national under-19 basketball team|Greece's Under-19 national team]] tryout camp. He turned out to be a vital addition to the team, as he went on to record 15.9 [[Point (basketball)|points]] and 5.0 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game, and also lead the team in minutes played. The Greek team went 5–2. After winning their first 5 games, they fell to the [[USA national under-19 basketball team|U.S.A.]] in a tight [[Single-elimination tournament|semifinal]],<nowiki/> and later lost in the [[Bronze Medal Game|bronze medal game]] to [[Turkey men's national under-18 and under-19 basketball team|Turkey]]. He was voted onto the tournament's All-Tournament Team, despite his team not earning a spot on the medals [[podium]].

On 6 June 2016, Dorsey was named to the senior men's [[Greek national basketball team]]'s 16 man preliminary training camp roster for the [[2016 FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament – Turin|2016 Turin FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament]]. However, he did not make the actual 12 man roster that would compete at the tournament.<ref>[http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/272199/greek-nt-squad-for-oqt-is-announced Greek NT squad for OQT is announced.]</ref>

==Personal life==
Dorsey acquired dual citizenship (full citizenship with both the [[United States]] and [[Greece]]) and a Greek [[passport]], due to his mother's Greek background. Dorsey's mother was born to a Greek father and Israeli mother, and her Greek surname is Konstantinidou.
